title: Personnel of the third band, the 1934 band that never recorded
summary: Randolph struggles to recall the sidemen: Barnett, the Oldhams, Leon Washington, Dunlap, Milton Fletcher, Prentice McCarey, and a guitarist who doubled bassoon.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Okay, who was in that third band, that never recorded?
The third band. Oh, I wish that band could have recorded.
It was a good one, huh?
Yes. I had drums -- Richard Barnett,
he's gone. He was a drummer, he's dead. Bill Oldham on bass violin, his brother on alto, the boy that's on tenor, he's dead now -- Leon Washington.
Red Washington,
Leon Washington, yes, (inaudible).
Yeah, he used to be with Red Saunders.
Yes.
Jazz -- that's Mike's -- what we called him. Wait a minute -- Dunlap, his name's Dunlap. We called him --
(End of Side One, Tape 4.)
Mike McKendrick's brother,
You called him Jazz. What did he play?
Trombone.
Trombone, yeah.
And Mike McKendrick was in the rhythm section.
Wait a minute--
Yes. (Unintelligible.)
Who was all playing?
Font
And I think we had -- we had Eddie Pannan, too, again.
On trumpet.
On -- no, on trombone.
Trombone, that's right.
what else Seville
Now, the trumpets was -- oh, my goodness, (inaudible), had Seover Brown on saxophone, --
He's a repeat from the '33 band.
Yes, he played alto. Let me see, did I have Scovell Brown?
You mentioned earlier that you had Budj--
Budd Johnson?
Budd Johnson in this band.

Well, no, this was one when I rehearsed at the Sunset. That's where I got this band together, at the Sunset. When I had Milton Fletcher on trumpet, and I can't recall the other boy's name, might come to me (inaudible). Again, Milton Fletcher was on trumpet, Prentice McCarey on piano, and -- who did I have on the other tenor? Because I wanted to get Pettiford from Pettifoss Minneapolis, one of the Pettifoss Brothers. A whale of a tenor man.
Pettiford? Oscar Pettiford's brother?
Yeah, Oscar Pettiford's brother.
That Oscar -- I think he played -- The Pettiford band, the family band.
Yes, uh-huh. Well, how many is that? Pettiford -- no, I mean Prentice McCarey on piano, Richard Barnett on drums, Bill Oldham on bass, --
And Mike?
No, I didn't have Mike McKendrick on -- I think I had Thomas, I forget his name, forget all the (unintelligible) boys' names.
named Thomas on guitar and bassoon.
Bassoon?
Yeah, guitar and bassoon. Because I know, in that arrangement, in Louis' theme song, I had a dialog between the brass and the bassoon, had a symphony right there, going on.
Uh-huh.

Now I got to put that -- now I got that rhythm together, I have the two trombones, and the -- Milton Fletcher on trumpet and -- can't recall that other fellow, trumpet -- all I know he's kind of a tall fellow, but I can't get his name. He was on trumpet. All right, and that was just about -- that was about the band.
So you had five brass and three saxes and four rhythm and Louis.
Yes. I'm just wondering if I didn't have the other tenor man. I was just wondering -- I'm trying to think who that other tenor man. We had an arrangement --
There were three or four saxes.
